1.1: Paul a seruaunt of God, and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of Gods elect, and the acknowledging of the trueth, which is according unto godlines,
1.2: Unto the hope of eternal life, which God that cannot lie, hath promised before the world began:
1.3: But hath made his word manifest in due time through the preaching, which is committed unto me, according to the commandement of God our Sauiour:
1.4: To Titus my natural sonne according to the common faith, Grace, mercie and peace from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ our Sauiour.
1.5: For this cause left I thee in Creta, that thou shouldest continue to redresse the thinges that remain, and shouldest ordeine Elders in every citie, as I appointed thee,
1.6: If any be vnreproueable, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, which are not slandered of riot, neither are disobedient.
1.7: For a Bishop must bee vnreproueable, as Gods steward, not froward, not angrie, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthie lucre,
1.8: But harberous, one that loveth goodness, wise, righteous, holy, temperate,
1.9: Holding fast that faithful word according to doctrine, that he also may bee able to exhort with wholesome doctrine, and convince them that say against it.
1.10: For there are many disobedient and vain talkers and deceivers of mindes, chiefly they of the Circumcision,
1.11: Whose mouthes must bee stopped, which subuert whole houses, teaching things, which they ought not, for filthie lucres sake.
1.12: One of themselves, even one of their own prophets said, The Cretians are alwaies liars, evil beastes, slow bellies.
1.13: This witness is true: wherefore convince them sharply, that they may be sound in ye faith,
1.14: And not taking heed to Jewish fables and commandements of men, that turn away from the trueth.
1.15: Unto the pure are all things pure, but unto them that are defiled, and vnbeleeuing, is nothing pure, but even their mindes and consciences are defiled.
1.16: They profess that they know God, but by works they deny him, and are abominable and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.

2.1: But speak thou the thinges which become wholesome doctrine,
2.2: That the elder men be watchful, grave, teperate, sound in the faith, in love, and in patience:
2.3: The elder women likewise, that they be in such behauiour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not subiect to much wine, but teachers of honest things,
2.4: That they may instruct the yong women to be sober minded, that they love their husbands, that they love their children,
2.5: That they be temperate, chaste, keeping at home, good and subiect unto their husbands, that the word of God be not evil spoken of.
2.6: Exhort yong men likewise, that they bee sober minded.
2.7: In all things shew thy self an ensample of good woorkes with vncorrupt doctrine, with grauitie, integritie,
2.8: And with the wholesome woorde, which can not be condemned, that hee which withstandeth, may be ashamed, having nothing concerning you to speak evil of.
2.9: Let servants be subiect to their masters, and please them in al things, not answering again,
2.10: Neither pickers, but that they shew al good faithfulness, that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Sauiour in all things.
2.11: For that grace of God, that bringeth salvation unto all men, hath appeared,
2.12: And teacheth us that we should denie vngodlinesse and worldly lusts, and that we should live soberly and righteously, and godly in this present world,
2.13: Looking for that blessed hope, and appearing of that glorie of that mightie God, and of our Sauiour Jesus Christ,
2.14: Who gave him self for us, that hee might redeem us from all iniquitie, and purge us to bee a peculiar people unto himself, zealous of good woorkes.
2.15: These things speak, and exhort, and convince with all authoritie. See that no man despise thee.

3.1: Put them in remembrance that they bee subiect to the Principalities and powers, and that they bee obedient, and ready to every good woorke,
3.2: That they speak evil of no man, that they be no fighters, but soft, shewing all meekenesse unto all men.
3.3: For wee our selves also were in times past unwise, disobedient, deceived, serving the lustes and divers pleasures, living in maliciousnes and enuie, hateful, and hating one another:
3.4: But when that bountifulness and that love of God our Sauiour toward man appeared,
3.5: Not by the woorkes of righteousness, which we had done, but according to his mercie he saved us, by the washing of the new birth, and the renewing of the holy Ghost,
3.6: Which he shed on us aboundantly, through Jesus Christ our Sauiour,
3.7: That we, being justified by his grace, should be made heires according to the hope of eternal life.
3.8: This is a true saying, and these thinges I will thou shouldest affirm, that they which have beleeued God, might be careful to shew foorth good woorkes. These things are good and profitable unto men.
3.9: But stay foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and brawlings about the Law: for they are unprofitable and vain.
3.10: Reiect him that is an heretike, after once or twise admonition,
3.11: Knowing that hee that is such, is perverted, and sinneth, being damned of his own self.
3.12: When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to mee unto Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.
3.13: Bring Zenas the expounder of the Law, and Apollos on their journey diligently, that they lack nothing.
3.14: And let ours also learn to shew foorth good woorkes for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.
3.15: All that are with mee, salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace bee with you all, Amen.  To Titus, elect the first bishoppe of the Church of the Cretians, written from Nicopolis in Macedonia.

56:1:1: Of those whom God hath chosen.

He voucheth his Apostleship, (not for Titus, but for the Cretans’ sake) both by the testimony of his outward calling, and by his consent wherein he agreeth with all the elect from the beginning of the world.
Minister, as Christ himself, in that that he was a minister and head of the Prophets, is called a servant, Isa. 43:10.

The faith wherein all the elect consent, is the true and sincere knowledge of God, tending to this end, that worshipping God aright that they at length obtain life everlasting according to the promise of God, who is true, which promise was exhibited to Christ in due time according to his eternal purpose.
56:1:2: Hope is the end of faith.
Freely, and of his mere liberality.
56:1:3: This truth is no other where to be sought, but in the preaching of the Apostle.
This word (Savior) doth not only signify a preserver of life, but also a giver of life.
56:1:4: There is but one way of salvation, common both to the Pastor and the flock.

The Apostle moveth the Cretans to hear Titus, by setting forth his consent and agreement with him in the faith, and therewithal showeth by what special note we may distinguish true ministers from false.
56:1:5: The first admonition, to ordain Elders in every city.
56:1:6: This word is proper to horses and oxen, which will not abide the yoke.
56:1:7: Not hard conditioned, and evil to please.
The second admonition, what faults pastors (whom he comprehended afore under the word Elders) ought to be void of, and what virtues they ought to have.
Whom the Lord hath appointed steward of his gifts.
56:1:8: Circumspect, of a sound judgment, and of a singular example of moderation.
56:1:9: The fourth admonition: To apply the knowledge of true doctrine unto use, which consisteth in two things, to wit, in governing them which show themselves apt to learn, and confuting the obstinate.
The third admonition: The Pastor must hold fast that doctrine, which the Apostles delivered, and pertaineth to salvation, leaving all curious and vain matters.
56:1:10: An applying of the general proposition to a particular: The Cretans above all others need sharp reprehensions: both because their minds are naturally given to lies and slothfulness, and also because of certain covetous Jews, which under a color of godliness joined partly certain vain traditions, and partly old ceremonies with the Gospel.
Of the Jews, or rather of those Jews, which went about to join Christ and the Law together.
56:1:12: Epimenides, who was counted a Prophet amongst them. Look upon Laertius and Cicero in his first book of Divination.
56:1:13: Roughly and plainly, and go not about the bush with them.
56:1:15: If our minds and conscience be unclean, what cleanness is there in us before regeneration?

He showeth in few words, that purity consisteth not in any external worship, and that that is according to the old Law, (as in difference of meats, and washing, and other such things which are abolished) but in the mind and conscience: and whosoever teach otherwise, know not what is true religion indeed, and also are nothing less than that they would seem to be.
56:2:1: The fifth admonition: The doctrine must not only be generally pure, but also be applied to all ages and orders of men, according to the diversity of circumstances.
56:2:2: What are the chiefest virtues for old and young, both men and women: and how they ought to be stirred up unto them continually.
56:2:7: Not such a gravity as may drive men from coming to the minister, but such as may cause them to come in most reverent and honest sort.
The sixth admonition: That both the Pastor’s life and doctrine must be sound.
56:2:9: Which may be done without offense to God.
The seventh admonition, of servants’ duty toward their masters.
56:2:11: The eighth admonition belonging to all the godly, that seeing God calleth all men to the Gospel, and Christ hath so justified us, that he hath also sanctified us, we must all of us give ourselves to true godliness and righteousness, setting before us a sure hope of that immeasurable glory: which thing must in such sort be beaten into their heads, that the gainsayers also must be reproved, by the authority of the mighty God.
56:2:12: Lusts of the flesh, which belong to the present state of this life and world.
56:2:13: Christ is here most plainly called that mighty God, and his appearance and coming is called by the figure Metonymy, our hope.
56:2:14: As it were a thing peculiarly laid up for himself.
56:3:1: He declareth particularly and severally, that which he said before generally, noting out certain chief and principal duties, which men owe to men, and especially subjects to their magistrates.
56:3:3: He confirmeth again the former exhortation, by propounding the free benefit of our regeneration, the pledge whereof is our Baptism.
56:3:5: Which the virtue of the holy Ghost worketh.
Word for word, of works which are done in righteousness: and this place doth fully refute the doctrine of merits.
56:3:8: Give themselves earnestly unto good works.
Again with great earnestness he beateth into our heads, how that we ought to give ourselves, to true godliness, and eschew all vain questions, which serve to nothing but to move strife and debate.
56:3:10: The ministers of the word must at once cast off heretics, that is, such as stubbornly and seditiously disquiet the Church, and will give no ear to Ecclesiastical admonitions.
56:3:12: Least of all, he writeth a word or two of private matters and commendeth certain men.
